rationale: The candidate reads as one compact dominant mass with a legible carved central void and a consistent stepped/roofed upper profile across views, so it is coherent in more than one projection and does not visibly collide across views. The parcel is respected as a contained, rotated footprint rather than a box-filling extrusion, and the blue access edge is answered by a clear open seam/void along the street-facing side. The silhouette is not an arbitrary stair-stack; it behaves more like a continuous inhabited section with a central cut. Programmatically, it plausibly supports neighborhood living / small mixed-use: there is an active ground threshold, a public interior void, and enough upper hierarchy for compact capacity. The main weakness is that the roof/upper mass is still somewhat generic and could better articulate the section-program relationship, but this is not severe enough to fail program fit.
